steps.title: Find and stage the client's files
do: Paul has given his permission for this in advance (see the access page): connect to his computer's Folder 1 `~/liferisk.co.za/Company - Paul` and Folder 2 `~/liferisk.co.za/Company - WR Clients/Paul Kafentzis (Client Files)`. Call get_device_info; if they are not connected, call device_request_folder_access ONCE with exactly those two paths (never the whole `~/liferisk.co.za`); then list the client's `2. Fact Find` folder under each and STAGE the files (exact copies). If the request is refused, do not retry: use the Microsoft 365 connector (PDF and Word files in page ranges), then Zapier. Never ask Paul to attach a file. Run only the commands this program shows you: no cp, sed, heredocs, and never open the program's own files.

You need: the form's two files in the client's `2. Fact Find` folder (`Fact Find (Audio to Text) - DD.MM.YYYY - Name Surname`: the .json and the .pdf), the Teams meeting transcript(s) in the same folder, and the latest Overview in `1. Overview` (reference only). Open every candidate: identify files by what is INSIDE, not by their names.

Register what you found (a missing optional file is told plainly, with where you looked): python3 {scripts}/run.py files {run} --form "<the .json>" [--formpdf "<the .pdf>"] --transcript "<transcript file>" [--transcript "<second file of the same meeting>"] [--overview "<file>"] [--missing "<what is not found and where you looked>"] [--copied "<files you had to type out from text>"]

The program checks the files itself (the form recognised by its content and its schema, the transcript complete). If it prints STOP, give Paul that one line and stop. A couple in one meeting is two runs: see the rules page.
steps.proof: the form's data file, its schema and the transcript(s) were checked by the program

steps.title: Read the form (both files)
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py form {run}

The program reads the data file AND the PDF, and prints what you must act on: the status counts, the preset/heard/verify values, the amounts only the PDF holds (the form works them out), notes that need cleaning, the company look-up verdict and the rows still empty. Read that printout in full: it is your list for the next steps.
steps.proof: form_read.json exists (the program has read the form)

steps.title: Read the transcript once, accurately
do: {chunk_commands}

Read every chunk in FULL, in order. At the end of each chunk the program names a line from the MIDDLE of it: the next command needs the first 5 words of that line (--seen), so the chunk must really be read. Never cut a chunk short (no tail, head, grep or loops) and never skip one. The last command closes the reading. Searching for keywords is not reading. While you read, keep a list of what the call says that the form lacks, gets wrong or contradicts: you write it down in step 5.
steps.proof: every chunk was served in full and in order, and every reading check passed

steps.title: Contact details and the lead source
do: Find the contact details (the form first, then the call, then the client's documents) and the lead source: search Outlook for the D&R Marketing appointment email (see the rules page).

Record the result: python3 {scripts}/run.py lead {run} --found --received DD/MM/YYYY --ref "<email subject>" --quote "<the line that shows it>"   or   --none "<what you searched and where>"   or   --unavailable "<what failed on every route>"

steps.title: Combine the form and the call into ONE report
do: Run once to see what is still empty (an empty overlay is fine): python3 {scripts}/run.py combine {run}

Then write {run}/overlay.json (format on the page below): fill every gap the form leaves from the call, the Overview and the client's documents; add the call's context (reasons, who pays what, timing, plans); record EVERY contradiction between the form and the call or a document: SORTED (a rule settles it, say which) or HIGHLIGHTED (both values and where each came from). Before leaving a row 'Not discussed', search the call, the Overview and the documents for it.

Every entry needs a source: the call's exact words ([{"line": 12, "quote": "exact words"}]) or a named document. The program checks that a quoted call line really is in the transcript. Run the combine command again after every change until it prints COMBINED with nothing left to settle.
steps.proof: content.json combined from the current overlay, quotes found in the transcript, no quote request without its insurer and basis

steps.title: Build the Fact Find Transcript PDF and look at it
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py build {run}
Open the page images ({run}/out/page-*.png) and look at every page: headings, tables, nothing cut off, notes in point form, no stray labels.
Record what you saw: python3 {scripts}/run.py look {run} --saw "<what you saw on the pages>"
steps.proof: the PDF is built from the current content and the page images were looked at

steps.title: Save into the client's folder, show Paul, get his OK
do: Save the PDF ({run}/out/<the file>) into the client's own `2. Fact Find` folder (the folder the form's files are in) with the device bridge's file tools. List the folder back and read the file's size from the listing.

Record it: python3 {scripts}/run.py saved {run} --folder "<the folder path>" --listed-size <bytes shown in the listing>. The listed size must equal the built file's size; if it does not, commit it again and list again.

Show Paul in ONE reply: the PDF (send it in the chat) and the short source report the program prints with `run.py report {run}`. This is the ONE stop: WAIT for his OK. If he corrects anything, change overlay.json, run combine, build, look, save again and show again (the program re-opens those steps by itself).
When Paul says it is right: python3 {scripts}/run.py ok {run} --paul-said "<his words>"
steps.proof: the saved size equals the built PDF and Paul's OK is recorded

steps.title: Summary, Planner note and the message to Sitamah
do: Without asking anything: (a) run the `fact-find-summary` skill on the saved Fact Find Transcript PDF; (b) run the `client-teams-transcript-skill` for this meeting: it makes the Planner note page and posts the message to Sitamah in Teams once, automatically (through Zapier).

Record what each made: python3 {scripts}/run.py chain {run} --summary "<Summary file name saved>" --planner "<link of the Planner page, or 'fallback text: why'>" --sitamah "<posted: message id | already_sent: where | failed: why>"
The program then prints the SHORT audit. Your reply is the three outputs, the message that was posted and that audit, unedited.
steps.proof: the Summary, the Planner note and the Sitamah message are recorded
